IDEA: Roster-transaction rules engine for front office staff deciding daily on option, DFA, IL placement, and call-up moves; software encodes MLB roster rules (options remaining, 40-man status, service-time thresholds, IL minimums, Rule 5 restrictions) and flags illegal or costly sequences before submission.
ASSUMPTION: Roster rules are publicly documented in the CBA and MLB rules materials, and could be encoded and checked against public transaction logs.
ASSUMPTION: The value comes from avoided errors and faster scenario comparison, not new information, so it may matter only on rare high-cost days.
ASSUMPTION: Sophisticated clubs, including the Cubs, likely already have internal tools or experienced staff who do this reliably.
UNKNOWN: cubs_existing_roster_compliance_tooling
UNKNOWN: historical_frequency_of_costly_roster_errors_league_wide
IDEA: Bullpen availability ledger for coaching staff deciding before each game which relievers are usable; software combines recent pitch counts, consecutive days pitched, warm-up-only sessions, and travel into one availability view.
ASSUMPTION: Public box scores capture game pitch counts but not bullpen warm-ups, so the useful version depends on internally logged data that is not publicly available.
ASSUMPTION: A shared whiteboard or spreadsheet maintained by the bullpen coach may already be enough; software adds value only if it reduces handoff errors.
UNKNOWN: whether_warmup_pitches_are_currently_logged_by_cubs
UNKNOWN: measured_relationship_between_unlogged_warmups_and_reliever_performance
IDEA: Minor-league promotion decision support for player development staff deciding at intervals whether a prospect should move up a level; software normalizes public minor-league stats by league, park, and age-relative-to-level, and tracks how stable a small sample is.
ASSUMPTION: Public minor-league data (box scores, some public Statcast for Triple-A) is lawfully accessible and detailed enough to give a useful baseline.
ASSUMPTION: Promotion decisions depend heavily on non-statistical factors (development goals, roster need, makeup) that software cannot capture.
ASSUMPTION: Sophisticated clubs likely already have proprietary minor-league tracking and translation models that outperform anything built from public data.
UNKNOWN: predictive_validity_of_public_minor_league_translations
UNKNOWN: cubs_internal_promotion_criteria
IDEA: Draft-board consistency checker for scouting directors deciding pick order during the draft; software detects internal inconsistencies (cross-checker grades vs. model rank vs. signability) and simulates which players are likely gone by each pick.
ASSUMPTION: Public mock drafts and historical draft position data could approximate the availability model, though accuracy is uncertain.
ASSUMPTION: The core inputs (scouting grades, signability conversations) are private and would have to stay internal; no Cubs scouting data should be invented.
UNKNOWN: accuracy_of_public_mock_drafts_for_availability_prediction
UNKNOWN: bonus_pool_value_for_cubs_current_draft_position
IDEA: Travel and sleep-schedule planner for performance staff deciding on flight times, arrival plans, and early-game workloads after long trips or time-zone changes; software combines the public MLB schedule, distances, and time-zone shifts into a fatigue-exposure calendar.
ASSUMPTION: The schedule and travel distances are public, but individual sleep or biometric data is private and must not be assumed or invented.
ASSUMPTION: Published research on travel and circadian effects in sports may suggest an effect, but its size and relevance to the Cubs are unverified.
UNKNOWN: effect_size_of_travel_fatigue_on_mlb_performance
UNKNOWN: cubs_schedule_flexibility_given_league_constraints
IDEA: Pitch-clock and pickoff-limit tracker for game-day staff and baserunning coaches deciding in real time whether to send a runner; software shows the current pitcher's remaining disengagements and his historical tendency to step off when limits are reached.
ASSUMPTION: Disengagement counts can be tracked manually from the broadcast or the dugout, and historical tendencies could be derived from public play-by-play.
ASSUMPTION: Teams may restrict electronic devices in the dugout, which could limit real-time delivery.
UNKNOWN: mlb_dugout_technology_rules_for_this_use
UNKNOWN: whether_public_data_records_disengagements_at_sufficient_granularity
IDEA: Contract and arbitration comparables explorer for front-office analysts deciding on extension offers and arbitration filing numbers; software retrieves historical public comparable cases by service time, position, and platform stats.
ASSUMPTION: Public contract and arbitration databases exist and could be used under their terms of service, but completeness and accuracy are unverified.
ASSUMPTION: An existing public tool or a spreadsheet may already be sufficient; custom software adds little unless it is tied to internal projections.
ASSUMPTION: Sophisticated clubs likely already have mature arbitration modeling.
UNKNOWN: terms_of_service_for_public_contract_databases
UNKNOWN: cubs_upcoming_arbitration_eligible_players
IDEA: Injury-return progression log for medical and performance staff deciding when a rehabbing player advances to the next stage; software records progression milestones and alerts when steps are skipped or timelines drift from the plan.
ASSUMPTION: All underlying medical data is private and protected, so this would be built only on internal or synthetic data, never invented Cubs records.
ASSUMPTION: The value lies in process reliability across staff handoffs, not prediction.
UNKNOWN: existing_cubs_medical_record_system_capabilities
UNKNOWN: privacy_and_regulatory_requirements_for_athlete_health_data
IDEA: Defensive substitution and platoon matchup sheet for the manager deciding late-game substitutions; software precomputes bench options against likely opposing relievers using public handedness splits and defensive metrics, with uncertainty bands shown.
ASSUMPTION: Public splits and defensive metrics are accessible, but small samples make many matchups noisy, so uncertainty must be shown explicitly.
ASSUMPTION: A printed card prepared by analysts before the game may already be sufficient, which makes this a low-novelty idea.
UNKNOWN: sample_size_thresholds_where_platoon_splits_become_reliable
IDEA: International amateur signing tracker for international scouting staff deciding on budget allocation across signing periods; software tracks bonus pool spending, commitments, and pool trades within league rules.
ASSUMPTION: International pool rules are public, while commitment details are private and must not be invented.
ASSUMPTION: A well-maintained spreadsheet likely suffices for a single club.
UNKNOWN: current_international_signing_rules_for_relevant_period
IDEA: Video clip retrieval index for hitting and pitching coaches deciding what to show a player before or after a game; software indexes the club's own video by pitch type, location, and outcome so clips can be retrieved quickly.
ASSUMPTION: Commercial video platforms that many clubs already license may already provide this, which would make custom software unnecessary.
ASSUMPTION: Public pitch-level data could be joined to video timestamps only if the club has the rights to that video.
UNKNOWN: capabilities_of_cubs_current_video_platform
UNKNOWN: coach_time_currently_spent_searching_video
IDEA: Data-quality monitoring for analysts deciding whether to trust daily model outputs; software detects missing games, schema changes, and implausible tracking values in incoming feeds before they reach decision makers.
ASSUMPTION: This is a boring but useful intervention whose value comes from avoided errors in downstream models.
ASSUMPTION: Mature analytics departments likely already have some pipeline validation.
UNKNOWN: frequency_of_data_feed_errors_affecting_decisions
IDEA: Weather-delay and doubleheader contingency planner for game-day operations and pitching staff deciding whether to start, delay, or reschedule; software combines public forecasts with pitcher-usage implications of a suspended or delayed game.
ASSUMPTION: Public weather forecasts are lawfully accessible, but the final postponement decision rests partly with the league and umpires, which limits club control.
ASSUMPTION: This partly overlaps the already explored Wrigley microclimate family and should be evaluated for distinctness.
UNKNOWN: club_vs_league_authority_over_postponement_decisions
IDEA: Places where software is likely unnecessary: one-off trade evaluations, staff scheduling, and simple leaderboard lookups, where public sites, spreadsheets, or manual processes already suffice.
ASSUMPTION: The cost of building and maintaining custom tools exceeds the value when decisions are infrequent or public tools already answer the question.
UNKNOWN: internal_cost_of_building_and_maintaining_custom_tools
IDEA: Places where sophisticated clubs likely already hold the advantage: pitch design, biomechanics, proprietary tracking-based player valuation, and projection systems, where an outside public-data tool is unlikely to add marginal value.
ASSUMPTION: Large-market clubs, including the Cubs, likely invest in these areas, but the extent of Cubs-specific investment is unverified.
UNKNOWN: cubs_analytics_department_size_and_capabilities

ASSUMPTION: Schedule-derived fatigue proxies predict performance or injury risk enough to change rest decisions without using private biometric data.

ASSUMPTION: Public Statcast spray and outcome data is sufficient for positioning recommendations that comply with the shift rules.

IDEA: Waiver-wire and minor-league free agent triage feed for pro scouting that ranks newly available players by public skill indicators (for example pitch-level metrics) against current organizational depth gaps, used for daily claim decisions.
ASSUMPTION: Public pitch-tracking metrics carry enough signal on fringe players to beat ad hoc review.

UNKNOWN: historical_value_of_waiver_claims_relative_to_cost

IDEA: Pitcher mechanics or arsenal drift monitor for player development that compares a club pitcher's public release point, velocity, and movement data against their own baseline to prompt coaching or medical check-ins.
ASSUMPTION: Drift in public tracking data precedes performance decline or injury often enough to warrant alerts, which is unverified.
ASSUMPTION: Clubs with private biomechanics data likely already have stronger internal versions, so the value of a public-data version is limited to a backup or cross-check.
UNKNOWN: predictive_validity_of_public_release_and_velocity_drift_for_injury

IDEA: Game-day substitution rules assistant for the bench coach that tracks the current roster, used players, two-way player and position-player-pitching eligibility, and runner rules to prevent illegal or wasteful substitutions in late innings.
ASSUMPTION: Substitution errors or suboptimal late-game bench use happen often enough to matter, which is unverified.

UNKNOWN: frequency_of_substitution_errors_league_wide

IDEA: Knowledge-retention system for analysts and coaches that records past decisions, the information available at the time, and the outcomes, so the organization can audit its own process across staff turnover.

ASSUMPTION: A shared document or wiki may already provide most of the value without custom software.

IDEA: Non-intervention area: core projection systems and pitch-quality models, where well-resourced clubs likely already hold advantages from proprietary data, so a public-data entrant is unlikely to outperform them.
